recentItems.title: How math can help with health decisions | Sommer Gentry & Dorry Segev | TEDxNYU Langone Health
recentItems.description:
This husband-and-wife research team discusses how a little bit of math can help you with medical decisions and, along the way, introduces cutting-edge transplant advances. Dr. Sommer Gentry is a Professor in the Department of Surgery at NYU Grossman School of Medicine. She co-directs the Center for Surgical and Transplant Applied Research (C-STAR) at NYU Langone Health.

Dr. Dorry Segev is a Professor in the Departments of Surgery and Population Health at NYU Grossman School of Medicine. He is also the Vice Chair of the Department of Surgery and Surgical Sciences and he co-directs the Center for Surgical and Transplant Applied Research (C-STAR) at NYU Langone Health. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Power Of Legacy: What Will Your Story Be? | Julian Elphick-Smith | TEDxGosport
recentItems.description:
The present eclipses the past in so much of our modern world. We are the lesser for it. Our stories and those handed down to us have the power to transcend the prevailing NOW. 

Recent grandparenthood and a dedication of Thursdays to looking after the grandchildren led me to reflect on the role of the grandparent. It is so much more than entertaining the children and 'giving them back at the end of the day'. Grandparenthood gives the privilege of time to build a legacy: a legacy, beyond the material, of a familial and cultural kind. We communicate our legacy in our stories which confirm our humanity. Such secure roots are doubly important in a technological age of hyper immediacy, self-absorption and shortening attention spans. We should champion the long view and ask ourselves: what has the past shared with me? What story will I embody for the future? Born in Brighton, Julian feels most naturally at home by the sea. He has taught English in the Portsmouth and Gosport area for the greater part of four decades and now resides very happily in Gosport beside Portsmouth Harbour.  His family has largely joined him, sharing a passion for the history, setting and sense of community that characterises our home town. Julian is a mediaevalist by specialisation and will speak on the importance of our connection with the past. His life journey, however, has been a little more diverse and taken him from the late night studios of university radio, through the world of ‘big firm’ accountancy in the booming 1980s, to achingly active grandparenthood today. In spite of his enthusiasm for Old English, Latin, church architecture and croquet, children at home and at school ensure that he remains young at heart - at least! This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Individual spark to collective fire | Olamilekan Bamidele (King Pexxie) | TEDxLead City University
recentItems.description:
What happens when personal passion meets purpose? This talk traces the journey of how one person's ideas and creativity can spark something far bigger than themselves, inspiring others, mobilizing communities, and eventually shaping a collective movement or culture.

Drawing from a personal journey across law, brand strategy, hospitality, and content creation, this talk unpacks how a single conviction can grow into a system that connects people and creates real, lasting impact. It's a story of how combining law, media, and culture can build bridges between disciplines and, more importantly, between people, creating a ripple effect that reaches far beyond where it started.

If you've ever wondered how individual drive turns into community-driven change, this talk offers a firsthand look at what that process actually looks like. Bamidele Olamilekan is a renowned entertainment lawyer, prolific author, and dynamic speaker. As the Principal Partner at Lekan Bamidele & Co., he has carved a niche in entertainment law, consistently protecting the rights of creatives and representing artists, producers, and industry professionals in complex contract negotiations, intellectual property matters, and dispute resolution.

With an unwavering commitment to excellence, Bamidele is not only a legal strategist but also a mentor dedicated to shaping the next generation of lawyers. His passion for capacity building and knowledge-sharing has positioned him as a beacon of inspiration within the legal community.

A true powerhouse in the industry, Bamidele Olamilekan's stellar track record, legal acumen, and client-focused approach make him a trusted name in the legal landscape. His work continues to impact lives, set standards, and push boundaries in the entertainment law space and beyond. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The power of yet | Lucrezia M | TEDxCanadian School Milan
recentItems.description:
Lucrezia reflects on the subtle strength of self-belief, guiding us through how internal conviction can carry us through life's loudest doubts.
 Lucrezia has faced challenges through her studies and these moments led her to focus on this topic for her TED talk. The 'power of yet' resonated with her after researching ways to calmly revisit errors and areas to improve. She hopes to inspire others! recentItems.title: The surprising power of ‘we' | Kamsi Asuzu- Obumselu | TEDxLead City University
recentItems.description:
There's a difference between what we build alone and what we build together. Individual effort adds, but collaboration multiplies. This talk explores that shift, how bringing people, ideas, and disciplines together doesn't just add value, it raises it exponentially.

Through personal experience across law, media, and culture, this talk breaks down how collaboration turns isolated effort into collective momentum, and how the right connections can take an idea from a single spark to a system that carries far more than one person ever could alone.

It's a case for why "we" will always outperform "I," and what it actually takes to build something raised to that power. Kamsi Asuzu-Obumselu is a strategist, brand storyteller, and creative leader passionate
about designing spaces of meaning for young people to grow, lead, and create impact.
She currently serves as the CEO and Executive Director of Limitless Club, a fast-growing
movement equipping young people with the mindsets, skills, and communities to thrive
in life and leadership. Under her leadership, Limitless Club has reached over 5,000 young
people through programs, gatherings, and peer-led chapters that nurture
purpose-driven leadership and collective growth.
A dynamic thinker at the intersection of strategy, storytelling, and social impact, Kamsi
is the creative force behind The Roundtable, Limitless Club’s flagship annual convening
that brings together thousands of young professionals, entrepreneurs, creatives and
thought leaders to engage in deep, transformative conversations about purpose,
leadership, and the future. She has also led initiatives such as Navigating the Next, a
career mentorship program for university students in Nigeria, and the Limitless
Chapters network, a peer-driven community model that has become a case study in
sustainable youth leadership.
With over eight years of experience across youth empowerment, communications, and
impact-driven innovation, Kamsi has worked with organizations and brands to design
programs, craft narratives, and build ecosystems that translate vision into lasting
change. Her portfolio includes collaborations with entities such as
Beyond.Representation, YouTube Music, and the Lagos State Government, among
others.
At her core, Kamsi believes that leadership is not reserved for the few but cultivated in
community, that when young people are seen, equipped, and connected, they become
catalysts for a better world. Her work bridges strategy and soul, combining sharp
execution with a deep belief in human potential.
Kamsi is recognized for her thoughtful approach to leadership and her ability to
translate complex ideas into experiences that move people to think, connect, and act.
She speaks on themes of purpose, leadership, community, and youth development,
inspiring a generation to live from enough and build meaningfully, together. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: How to support loved ones with cancer | Dr.  Arif Kamal | TEDxRaleigh
recentItems.description: Many people facing a cancer diagnosis experience loneliness and social isolation.  In addition to worsening quality of life, such experiences are associated with shorter survival.  Few realize they hold a life-changing healing power through regular outreach in the form of audio and written communication.  We discuss that intentional, small-form efforts for connection can be rewarding to both allies of persons with cancer and the patients themselves, and can be achieved in as little as seconds a day.  Complemented with usual therapies provided by doctors, communities can work together to improve the lives of millions of people who seek more and better days during their cancer journey.  Dr. Arif Kamal is the inaugural chief patient officer for the American Cancer Society, a practicing oncologist and palliative care physician in North Carolina, and an associate professor of medicine and population health at the Duke University School of Medicine. He has published more than 225 peer-reviewed scientific articles and is recognized as an international expert in supportive oncology and palliative care This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Con-Ciencia: ¿Quién soy? | Alejandro Tapia de Jesús | TEDxUniversidad Iberoamericana CDMX
recentItems.description:
Vivimos rodeados de información, estímulos y ruido. Estamos tan acostumbrados a llenar cada silencio que hemos dejado de preguntarnos qué pasa cuando simplemente estamos con nosotros mismos.

Alejandro Tapia de Jesús nos invita a reflexionar sobre cómo construimos nuestra realidad, cómo interpretamos lo que nos sucede y cuánto de lo que somos está realmente en nuestras manos.

A través de ejercicios, una ilusión óptica, meditación e imaginación, la charla propone volver a lo esencial: reconocer lo que pensamos, sentimos y somos. En un mundo donde las redes sociales, las etiquetas y la tecnología ocupan cada vez más espacio en nuestra vida, la invitación es a recuperar nuestra atención, nuestra identidad y nuestra capacidad de imaginar.

Porque nuestra grandeza no está solamente en cuánto podemos brillar, sino en cuánto podemos iluminar a los demás. Keep looking at the stars. One day you will be there. Alejandro Tapia de Jesús, es Doctor en Investigación Psicológica por la Universidad Iberoamericana. Su línea de investigación es la plasticidad cerebral y los sistemas neuroquímicos, neurofisiológicos y neuropsicológicos implicados. Particularmente se centra en las conductas motivadas: alimentación, sexo y socialización; la actividad física y la salud mental, el uso de inteligencia artificial y la función cognitiva; y el envejecimiento y la reserva cognitiva. Ha contribuido en libros y artículos especializados en el área de las neurociencias, así como presentación en congresos nacionales e internacionales del área.

Obtuvo por dos años consecutivos la beca de investigación del Interdisciplinarx Research Training Institute on Hispanic Drug Abuse de la University of Southern California, donde ganó el premio "Best poster presentation by a young investigatar".

Es licenciado en Psicología por la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México. Maestro en Psicología (UNAM) con residencia en Neuropsicología Clínica con experiencia en evaluación, diagnóstico e intervención en pacientes con patologías neurológicas, alteraciones psiquiátricas y deterioro cognoscitivos asociado al envejecimiento y el TDAH. Tiene especialidad en neuropsicología deportiva y desarrolla programas de acondicionamiento
físico y mental para atletas.

Es académico de tiempo completo en el Departamento de Salud de la Universidad Iberoamericana, CDMX. Coordinador de la Maestría en Nutriología Aplicada. Ha impartido múltiples diplomados, talleres, cursos y conferencias en diversas instituciones nacionales e internacionales.

Finalmente pertenece al Sistema Nacional de Investigadores e Investigadoras This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Hey Everyone. I’m Katya the Destroyer | Katya Osei | TEDxAccra
recentItems.description: A journey through growing up, finding purpose, and learning that maybe the point isn’t to save the world but to help people believe it can be different. A story about Korle Lagoon, impossible things, and the power of asking: why not? Katia Osei, also known as Katya the Destroyer, is a Ghanaian engineer, researcher, and storyteller working to democratize the "-isms" and "-ologies" long reserved for the privileged few. After studying bioengineering at Harvard University, she returned to Ghana's coastline, a historic site where many of the stories that shaped today's unequal world were first told. Her work spans genetic engineering to community ecology, bridging conventional academia and citizen scence. Katia believes that the world as we know it was first spoken into being and that new stories, told from this same coast, can help unbuild it into something fairer. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What Africa's industrialists taught me | Emmanuel Osei Ntim | TEDxAccra
recentItems.description:
Partnership isn't a business strategy Africa's industrialists adopted; it is a stewardship tradition they inherited and scaled. The same logic that built Kwahu trading networks built Dangote's empire. If we want the next generation of African industrial giants, we have to stop celebrating solo founders and start deliberately building and teaching symbiosis. Emmanuel Osei Ntim leads FON Packaging Ventures, one of
Ghana's leading corrugated carton manufacturers, and founded
EON Investments. A proud Kwahu and the eldest of four brothers,
he grew up inside the family business his parents built from a
trading shop in Tudu, on the factory floor from the age of twelve.
Educated at Ghana International School and Bryant University in
Rhode Island, he was back at work in Accra within 48 hours of
graduating. Under his leadership, the company grew from an internal
supply solution into a manufacturer serving Nestlé, Wilmar and
Olam. Today he writes and speaks on African industrialization and
second-generation succession under the banner Manufacturing
Africa Forward. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What If the US Wasn't Colonised? | Holly Fitzpatrick | TEDxFrancis Holland School Sloane Square
recentItems.description: This talk explores the counterfactual question of what would have happened if large-scale colonisation had not occurred in the region which we now call the United States of America. This talk discusses how modern nations and borders are not inevitable, and are influenced by historical actions, political decisions, and geography.  Holly Fitzpatrick is a student in the Lower Sixth studying Politics, Economics and Religious Studies. She hopes to study International Relations at university. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What if corporations ran countries? | Jemima Gray | TEDxFrancis Holland School Sloane Square
recentItems.description: We all have called the government a number of colourful names at some point and most people mainly seem to focus on the negative aspects of a politicians career, painting most in a bad light. However, we largely do not apply the same attitudes to companies that arguably have the same influence and power as governments. So what if companies were running our governments. Would we be better off?  Jemima Gray is a student in the Lower Sixth studying Politics, English and History of Art. She hopes to study Politics and International Relations at university and has a particular interest in how governments define their international identity and their subsequent influence in global politics This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What if we could speak to animals? | Alice Chavarot | TEDxFrancis Holland School Sloane Square
recentItems.description: What if one of the most intelligent conversations on Earth has been happening underwater this whole time? This talk explores how artificial intelligence is being used to analyse sperm whale vocalisations, uncovering patterns that challenge the way we think about language, intelligence, and consciousness itself. Blending marine biology, AI, and philosophy, it asks a deeper question: if another species may possess a complex form of communication, what does that force us to reconsider about humanity’s place in the natural world? Alice Chavarot is a student in the Lower Sixth studying English Literature, Mathematics, Biology, and Spanish. She hopes to study Biology at University and is particularly interested in animal sciences. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
